name: Mexico City: training base scorecard
summary: Mexico City has deep boxing and MMA roots (Nuevo Jordan, Pancho Rosales, Romanza, Bonebreakers), but the open web gave little first-hand evidence on sparring or kickboxing and Muay Thai quality, so every gym needs a trial week. Live in Narvarte: Pancho Rosales is inside it, Del Valle and San Juan gyms (MD, Team Guerra) are a short ride away and rooms are cheaper than Roma or Condesa. No sea, and the city sits at about 2,240 m, which visitors say makes the first sessions hard.
dec_jan: Dry season in the highlands, so training is not weather disrupted. Gyms list Sunday closures and holiday hour changes, no December closure evidence found.

details.neighbourhoods: Narvarte Poniente: furnished rooms 6,300 to 8,350 MXN (about 2,400 to 3,200 DKK), listings on propiedades.com. Roma: 5,800 to 10,000 MXN, median 7,500 (about 2,850 DKK). Condesa and Hipodromo: 6,000 to 8,500 MXN. Centro and Doctores (Nuevo Jordan): room rents not found, a 2020 El Financiero piece put Doctores one-bedroom flats at 7,000 to 10,000 MXN. Borough average for a two bedroom flat in Aug 2026 was 29,149 MXN in Cuauhtemoc (Roma, Condesa, Doctores, Centro) against 20,486 MXN in Benito Juarez (Narvarte), so Narvarte is the cheaper base. name: Bosawás rainforest trip with Mayangna guides (Siuna)
summary: Bosawás is the largest rainforest reserve in Central America and a UNESCO biosphere reserve on the Honduras border. Entry needs a certified native guide and a free permit (Siuna, Bonanza or Peñas Blancas); you sleep in Mayangna or Miskitu village cabins and travel by river and trail.
season: Dry season January to April is best. May to December is rainy (peak August to October), rivers rise and trails and roads can close.
dec_jan: December is end of rainy season: muddy trails and high rivers; January is better.
price: Permit free. Guide and tour prices not published; arrange in Siuna or through an agency.
duration: 4 to 5 days minimum (1 to 2 days of travel each way)
requirements: Certified native guide and permit. Rain gear, boots, repellent, headlamp. Check vaccines (yellow fever, hepatitis A and B, malaria prophylaxis). Travel insurance.

details.access: Siuna (southwest, river trips), Waslala (cloud forest and highlands), Bonanza (hardest, most remote hikes)
details.getting_there: Managua to Siuna by bus about 10.5 h (Transporte El Venado, via Río Blanco) or La Costeña flight about 1 h
details.wildlife: Jaguar, puma and ocelot (mostly tracks), tapir, scarlet macaw, spider and howler monkeys, harpy eagle, hundreds of orchids
details.communities: Mayangna and Miskitu villages, homestay cabins, often no electricity; ask before photographing people
details.safety: Armed settlers (colonos) linked to cattle, logging and illegal gold mining attacked Mayangna and Miskitu communities in the reserve interior in 2020, 2021, 2022 and March 2023 (Wilú, Musawás, Sabakitang), with several killed. No reports of tourists targeted, but go only with an established local guide, stay away from mining areas and check current Danish (UM) and US advice for Nicaragua first.

what_people_say.quote: Independent entry is not allowed; a certified native guide and a permit are required.

name: Peñas Blancas cloud forest and waterfalls (edge of Bosawás)

summary: The easiest way into the Bosawás forest: a community eco-lodge and farm homestays on the cloud forest massif at the reserve's southern edge. Guided hikes to La Pavona waterfall, swimming streams, primary forest and quetzals at dawn, plus coffee farm life.
season: Year round; drier January to April.
dec_jan: Coffee harvest season in December and January, wet and cool in the forest.
price: Hikes about US$5 per person with a guide; lodge and homestay prices not published (book through the CEN).
requirements: Book ahead with the CEN (Centro de Entendimiento con la Naturaleza, Km 195 road to El Cuá, +505 470 7590). No alcohol or smoking in the community. Boots, rain gear, warm layer, flashlight.

details.getting_there: Managua to Matagalpa by microbus (hourly from Mercado Mayoreo), then bus from the Guanuca terminal toward El Cuá or Bocay, off at Empalme La Manzana (2.5 to 3 h)
details.hikes: La Pavona (1.5 to 2 h, hard, big waterfall), Piscina de las Guardatinajas (20 min, bathing stream), El Sonoro (20 min), El Horno (3 h, primary forest, camp for quetzals at dawn), El Cafetal (coffee farm)
details.wildlife: Monkeys, resplendent quetzal, orchids, tree ferns; jaguar present but rarely seen

area: Rincon del Mar, Tintipan and Mucura (Sucre and Bolivar)
summary: Fly Medellin Olaya Herrera to Tolu (1 h 10, from about 570 DKK, daily) and taxi 1 h, or bus 3 to 4 h from Cartagena for about 80 DKK. score.note: total is the plain mean of the four criteria

details.verdict: A real disconnect base with clear water and on-the-water beds, easiest by a cheap 70-minute flight from Medellin to Tolu. The weak spots are a thin long-stay backpacker crowd and limited nightlife, and the Colombian holiday rush from mid-December.
details.access: MDE (EOH) to TLU Satena or Clic nonstop 1 h 10, US$88 to 189 for 5 to 10 Dec 2026; BOG to TLU Satena Mon and Fri; no CTG to TLU flight. Tolu to Rincon taxi about 1 h. Cartagena bus to San Onofre plus mototaxi 3 to 4 h, about COP 40,000. Tranq It Easy boat Cartagena to the islands 09:00 daily, 2 h, COP 150,000 to 160,000.
details.water_and_lodging: Islands have the clearest water and Casa en el Agua sits on the reef. Rincon has several beachfront hostels (Blue Sea, Beach House, Mamallena, Dos Aguas, Merakai).
details.long_stay_crowd: Writers recommend 3 nights in Rincon; Casa en el Agua guests mostly stay 1 to 3 nights; Mucura is a day-trip beach.
details.food_and_bars: Rincon: La Negrita, Kapito Harri, Che, Canto del Caracol, El Refugio de Petra, Mar Blanco, Dubai, beach bars by Mamallena, Dos Aguas bar. Quiet nightlife. Islands: hostel kitchens and bars only.
details.village_life: About 4,000 people, one dirt main street, fishermen, friendly; no street lights.
details.utilities: No ATM in Rincon or on the islands (Tolu and San Onofre have them). Water outages and scarce water; occasional power cuts in Rincon; islands on solar or generators with bucket showers. Slow internet, Claro SIM helps.
details.safety: Writers felt safe day and night in Rincon. Do not arrive in San Onofre after dark. Check that night plankton boats carry lights.
details.dec_jan: Dry season starts; strong trade winds (brisas) from December to about March make boat crossings choppy. Colombian holiday crowds and higher prices mid-December to mid-January.

details.access: Satena EOH to Acandi about 1 h, COP 300,700 one way (614 DKK), then 25 min lancha. Charter EOH to CPB Mon, Wed, Sat from COP 400,000 (2024). Or bus MDE to Necocli 8 to 10 h plus 1.5 h boat (COP 85,000).

details.hike: Capurgana to Sapzurro over the hill about 1.5 h, muddy after rain; Sapzurro to La Miel (Panama) about 15 to 30 min up steps, passport needed, no stamp. Boat Capurgana to Sapzurro COP 10,000.
details.electricity: MinEnergia, 30 Jul 2025: first continuous 24 h power from a hybrid solar plant. Older guides report nightly cuts 05:00 to 09:00.
details.safety: Danish UM (Jun 2026) advises against all travel in Choco except Capurgana tourist area; Acandi town is not exempt. Clan del Golfo controls the wider Uraba and Darien. Guides call the tourist area safe; stay on marked trails.
